title: Quote of the day by investor Warren Buffett on AI capex: "That's real money... That kind of money wasn't even put in the railroad business" — outlining his bullish long-term thesis on AI
excerpt: AI companies are depleting their cash reserves and pouring historic levels of money into the AI buildout
content_html:
AI demands a huge amount of energy, water, compute, and, of course, money. Big tech companies, including Google and Meta, have pledged huge sums of money toward the capital expenditure (capex) to continue the push to more powerful AI. But many inventors feel increasingly wary that this spending is simply swelling an already inflated bubble.

Laying the tracks

Speaking with CNBC in July 2026, the legendary investor Warren Buffett, who recently retired, weighed in on the capex debate.

Quote of the day

This article is part of TechRadar Pro's QOTD project to provide an insight into the minds of the brightest and most recognized figures in the technology industry today and in years gone by. Read the full series here.

Big tech companies are pledging a huge sum to the AI infrastructure buildout, which may reach up to $750 billion over 2026 and up to $4.5 trillion by 2030 among the four largest hyperscalers, including Meta, Microsoft, Amazon, and Alphabet. Many suggest this is further evidence of a bubble being fuelled aggressively by big tech companies doubling down on a technology that hasn't demonstrated meaningful returns.

But explaining his firm Berkshire Hathaway's 17.85 million-share purchase of Alphabet stock, disclosed in November 2025, Warren Buffett drew parallels between this level of spending and that during the 1800s to build the railroad system.

From digital to physical

As an investor, Buffett famously avoided software giants, suggesting they were asset-light businesses and didn't see the value in the investment propositions. This is a point he's since conceded he was wrong about. The firm he led made an additional $10 billion investment in Alphabet in June 2026.

The rationale is that there's currently a pivot underway in which these companies are shifting from the purveyors of digital products, namely applications and software, toward the physical infrastructure and compute to power AI.

Although the hyperscalers have been investing heavily in cloud infrastructure to power their software as a service (SaaS) propositions, the spending that AI commands is on a completely different level, as the figures show. That's why, in the end, Buffett believes that Alphabet proved a sound investment – given he believes that they have the cash flow to sustain the ongoing physical infrastructure buildout.

铺设轨道

2026 年 7 月，最近退休的传奇投资者沃伦·巴菲特在接受 CNBC 采访时发表了对资本支出争论的看法。

当日报价

本文是 TechRadar Pro 的 QOTD 项目的一部分，旨在深入了解当今和过去几年技术行业中最聪明、最受认可的人物的想法。 在这里阅读完整系列。

大型科技公司承诺投入巨额资金用于人工智能基础设施建设，其中包括 Meta、微软、亚马逊和 Alphabet 在内的四大超大规模企业到 2026 年可能达到 7500 亿美元，到 2030 年将达到 4.5 万亿美元。 许多人认为，这进一步证明大型科技公司加倍投资一项尚未表现出有意义回报的技术，从而积极助长了泡沫。

但在解释 2025 年 11 月披露的伯克希尔哈撒韦公司购买 1785 万股 Alphabet 股票的情况时，沃伦·巴菲特将这一支出水平与 1800 年代建设铁路系统的支出进行了类比。

从数字到物理

作为一名投资者，巴菲特以避开软件巨头而闻名，他认为这些企业是轻资产企业，看不到投资主张的价值。 他后来承认这一点是错误的。 他领导的公司于 2026 年 6 月向 Alphabet 追加投资 100 亿美元。

其理由是，目前正在发生一个转变，这些公司正在从数字产品（即应用程序和软件）的供应商转向物理基础设施和计算以支持人工智能。

尽管超大规模企业一直在云基础设施上投入巨资，以支持其软件即服务 (SaaS) 主张，但如图所示，人工智能所要求的支出处于完全不同的水平。 这就是为什么巴菲特最终认为 Alphabet 被证明是一项明智的投资——因为他相信 Alphabet 有足够的现金流来维持正在进行的实体基础设施建设。
